2. FIR in Cr. No.0104/2016 was registered by the RMC Yard Police station, Yeshawanthapur for offences under Section 419, 420, 471, 468 r/w 34 of IPC.

Essentially allegation made in the said complaint is that when the complainants were abroad their NC: 2024:KHC:10870 signatures were fabricated and forged by the petitioners inducting herself as partner in M/s Rajalakshmi Industries constituting partnership and taking control over the partnership and in furtherance thereof, the properties belonging to the said firm were sold and it is in that background that action was sought to be taken.
Investigation having been completed, a charge sheet in C.C. No.24623/2017 was laid on 13.07.2017.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has filed a Suit in O.S.
No.3648/2016 for injunction against the complainant and others wherein an exparte injunction had been granted and as such, the proceedings are civil in nature and no criminal proceedings can be made out.

Respondent No.2 has also filed a suit in O.S. No.753/2018 seeking for injunction,
declaration and other reliefs, as such the dispute is civil in nature.
NC: 2024:KHC:10870 4.

In regard to the said suit, he submits that in O.S. No.753/2018 a declaration is sought for as regards the sale deed executed being nonest as also the induction of petitioner being nonest which is a civil remedy.,
5.
On the above grounds he submits that the reliefs sought for are to be granted.
6. Sri.N.P.Amruthesh, learned counsel for respondent- complainant would submit that the petitioner has forged the signature of the respondent in inducting herself into the partnership firm.
As such, he submits that the above petition is required to be rejected.

7. Heard Sri.Arvind Ghimiray, learned counsel for Sri.Joseph Anthony, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri.M.R.Patil, learned HCGP for respondent No.1 and Sri.N.P.Amruthesh, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused papers 8.

The points that would arise for consideration are:
NC: 2024:KHC:10870 a) Whether merely because civil suits are pending would a party be estopped or prohibited from taking action under the criminal law?
b) Can a complainant agitate both civil remedies and criminal remedies in the same set of facts and circumstances?

9. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that the petitioner has filed a suit in O.S.
No.3648/2016, the respondent has also filed a suit in O.S. No.753/2018, therefore, the matter is civil in nature.
Insofar suit in O.S. No.3648/2016, the same having been filed by the accused, the accused cannot merely on the basis of filing a suit contend that the disputes are civil in nature.
The mere filing of a civil suit by an accused cannot come to the rescue of the accused.

Insofar as suit in O.S. No.753/2018 is concerned, the same apparently has been filed for injunction, declaration and other reliefs as regards the induction of the petitioner as a partner relating to the sale deeds executed by the petitioner.

sentences.text: This in my considered opinion and as submitted by Sri.Amruthesh are civil remedies which the respondent would be entitled for negating the actions taken by the petitioner since it is only by an order of the Court that the same could be negated and set- aside.

Criminal proceedings being initiated for offences under the respective criminal enactments would not negate the action or the documents executed but only result in punishment of the accused, if found guilty.
Thus, I am of the considered opinion that filing of the suit would not debar the complainant from taking criminal action as regards offences if any made out under the criminal acts.

Hence, I answer points No.1 and 2 by holding that mere filing of a civil suit would not disentitle a complainant initiating criminal action and further that a party could resort to both criminal and civil proceedings if circumstances and facts so provide.
In view of discussion above and in the circumstances, no grounds having been made out, the petition stands dismissed.
